sections.title: Sound of letter tê
paragraphs: The name of this letter is (tê) /te/. It makes one single sound, heard in (tempo) /ˈtẽ.pu/, meaning time or weather.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Touch the back of your upper front teeth with the tip of your tongue. Stop the air completely for a brief moment. Release the tongue cleanly without puffing out a breath of air. Keep your vocal cords silent. You can hold your hand before your mouth to feel no burst of air.

sections.title: Reading rules
paragraphs: This letter always makes the sound /t/ in every position. You hear it at the end of (noite) /ˈnoj.tɨ/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: In English words like tea, you puff out air. Keep your breath back completely. Never turn this sound into the ch sound in cheap when an e follows. Place the tongue tip strictly against your upper teeth.
